surprises.head: Los Angeles’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Los Angeles’s power play created 16.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.6 (about 8.2 against San Jose) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Kempe bags a hat trick
paras: Kenny Connors picked up his first NHL point. Adrian Kempe got the scoring started for the Kings less than two minutes in. Kempe and Quinton Byfield scored two and a half minutes apart late in the first to push the lead to 3-0. Macklin Celebrini got the Sharks on the board on the power play early in the second, and Erik Haula extended the lead to 4-1 midway through the period. Kempe completed his hat trick on the power play less than five minutes later to make it 5-1. Joel Armia stretched the lead to 6-1 early in the third. Ivar Stenberg cut Los Angeles’ lead to 6-2 on the power play midway through the period, far too late to matter. Byfield scored his second of the night on the power play with less than six minutes left to make it 7-2 for the Kings. Artemi Panarin finished with four assists.

The Sharks had more of the shots, 32-26, but the Kings had the better ones. Darcy Kuemper, who gave up five goals against Ottawa in his last start, made 30 saves for the Kings, and Yaroslav Askarov allowed seven goals on 26 shots. Kuemper has won five straight starts.
The Kings went 3-for-5 on the power play. The Kings improved to 5-7-2, seventh in the Pacific, while the Sharks fell to 7-9-1, slipping to sixth in the Pacific.
